title: Global Uniqueness for the Smooth Isotropic Elasticity Inverse Problem
main_claim: On a bounded connected smooth domain in R^3, the full displacement-to-traction map determines smooth Lamé moduli (λ, μ) uniquely, provided μ>0 and 3λ+2μ>0. The proof has five steps. (1) Boundary determination gives a common exterior extension of the coefficients. (2) Exact physical solutions are transferred across ∂Ω. (3) An augmented (u, div u) system with Laplacian principal part gives a Carleman estimate, and exact CGO solutions realise a local transport frame. (4) Weak limits of the transferred amplitudes give a compactly supported comparison G that is holomorphic in the null direction. (5) Bundle rigidity on the null conic (H ≅ O(-1)^2) forces G = Id, and a finite-type Hessian ODE then recovers μ and λ.

issues.location: Lemma 2.1 (common exterior extension), use of Tan–Liu Theorem 1.2
issues.description: Boundary determination of the full jets of λ and μ comes entirely from the external citation (Tan–Liu Thm 1.2, with Nakamura–Uhlmann / Lin–Nakamura as alternatives). I could not check that theorem's exact hypotheses (positivity condition, dimension, smoothness) against the source. This is a dependency on the citation, not an identified error.
issues.evidence: Proof of Lemma 2.1: 'By Theorem 1.2 of Tan and Liu ... equality of the elastic Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps determines all boundary partial derivatives of both Lamé moduli. Our inequalities imply λ+μ>μ/3>0, so their positivity condition holds.'
